JUDGMENT

This appeal under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (the Act) has been filed by the third respondent/insurer in O.P. (MV) No.188/2016 on the file of the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal,
Kollam, (the Tribunal), aggrieved by the Award dated 29/06/2019.
The respondents herein are the claim petitioners and respondents 1 & 2 respectively in the original petition.
In this appeal, the parties and the documents will be referred to as described in the original petition.

2. According to the claim petitioners, the wife and children of deceased Suseelan, on 09/01/2016 at 09:00 p.m., the deceased was travelling through NH 47 as a pillion rider on motorcycle bearing Bharti Axa General Insurance Co.Ltd vs Bindhu on 10 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/99616168/
2 registration No.KL-02AH/5723 and when he reached the place by name Kappalandimukku, the scooter bearing registration No.KL-02AS/8511 ridden by the second respondent in a 2025:KER:40710 negligent manner knocked him down as a result of which he sustained grievous injuries, to which he succumbed.
3. The first respondent/owner and the second respondent/rider remained ex parte.
4. The third respondent/insurer filed written statement contending that the amount claimed was exorbitant.
It was also contended that there was no negligence on the part of the second respondent/rider.
5. Before the Tribunal, Exts.A1 to A12 were marked on the side of the claim petitioners.
No oral evidence was adduced by either side.

6. The Tribunal on consideration of the documentary evidence and after hearing both sides, found negligence on the part of the second respondent/rider of the offending vehicle resulting in the incident and hence awarded an amount of 21,44,700/- together with interest @ 8% per annum from the date of the petition till the date of realisation with proportionate costs.
Aggrieved by the Award, the third respondent/insurer has come up in appeal.
7. The only point that arises for consideration in this 2025:KER:40710 appeal is whether there is any infirmity in the findings of the Tribunal calling for an interference by this Court.
8. Heard the learned counsel for the appellant/insurer.
Though notice was served on the respondents, they have not appeared in person or through counsel.
9. The award of compensation by the Tribunal under the following heads are challenged by the claim petitioner - Notional income
The allegation in the petition is that the deceased, a tailor was earning 20,000/- per month.
The Tribunal fixed the notional income at 15,000/-.
It is submitted by the learned counsel for the third respondent/insurer that in the absence of any evidence, the amount fixed is high.

My attention is also drawn to the dictum in Ramachandrappa v. Manager, Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Co. Ltd, (2011) 13 SCC 236, where the income of a coolie in the year 2016 was fixed at 10,500/- per month.

entities.text: Ramachandrappa v. Manager, Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Co. Ltd, (2011) 13 SCC 236
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Hence, the argument advanced is that the notional income may be fixed accordingly.
It is true that no oral or documentary evidence was adduced 2025:KER:40710 to prove that the deceased was a tailor.
As relied on by the Tribunal, Ext. A11 inquest report shows that he was a tailor in Al manama fabrics.

That being the position, I find that fixing the notional income at 12,000/-
per month would be just and reasonable.
It is also brought to my notice that the correct multiplier that ought to have been applied is 14, but the Tribunal has wrongly applied 13 as the multiplier.

In the light of the dictum in Sarla Verma v.
Delhi Transport Corporation, (2009) 6 SCC 121 : AIR 2009 SC 3104 : 2010(2) KLT 802, I find that the multiplier to be applied will be 14.
